causal_graphs.context: PS I-retaining cells grown in BG-11 at 30 C and 40 umol photons per square meter per second; liquid culture at 120 rpm. Photoautotrophy omits glucose. Oxygen evolution uses intact cells at 5 ug chlorophyll/mL, a Clark electrode, 0.1 mM 2,5-dimethyl-p-benzoquinone and 0.5 mM potassium ferricyanide, illuminated above 580 nm at 1 mmol photons per square meter per second. The oxygen-assay temperature is not explicitly specified and parental maintenance atrazine is not assigned to this assay. Table 2 reports means and SD from three independent experiments.

edges.mechanism: Rg2 grows photoautotrophically with doubling time 13.3 +/- 0.5 h, whereas the T192H parent does not grow under that condition. Transfer of the suppressor-region PCR fragment also restores photoautotrophic growth to T192H. The effect is conditional on the tested genetic background and does not resolve a direct DUF58 folding or degradation mechanism.

edges.mechanism: In the specified intact-cell assay, Rg2 oxygen evolution is 275 +/- 35 umol O2 per mg chlorophyll per hour versus 0 in T192H. WT is 256 +/- 28 and WT-D2-restored T192T/Y294Stop is 248 +/- 32. This supports recovery from the T192H defect, not enhancement over WT or an isolated-domain reaction. Oxygen evolution and growth are parallel measured outcomes, not an experimentally resolved causal chain between them.
edges.subject: rg2-slr2013-y294stop-t192h

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Slr2013 is UniProtKB:P73233 (NCBIProtein:BAA17260.1), a 435-residue Kazusa reference, taxon 1111708, sequence version 1. UniProt and InterPro sequences agree; PF01882 maps at 195-385 inclusive and reference residue 294 is Y. The stop predicts retention of residues 1-293, including DUF58 residues 195-293, and loss of residues 294-435, including the remaining domain and a C-terminal extension. This is neither a whole-domain deletion nor proof of domain sufficiency. The laboratory PCC 6803 substrain is not equated with the complete Kazusa reference genome.
causal_graphs.limitations: Genomic-fragment mapping and transfer of a PCR-amplified mutant region support the suppressor attribution, but an independently reconstructed single-base allele and reciprocal full-length Slr2013 rescue are not established here. The mapped region contains additional genes and possible cotranscription. The predicted 293-residue product was not directly measured here. Restoring WT D2 while retaining Y294Stop yields near-WT growth and oxygen evolution; other tested D2 mutants were not rescued. Chaperone and protease interpretations remain alternatives, not demonstrated direct chemistry.

evidence.explanation: Methods, Table 2, mapping and deletion Results, alternate D2 backgrounds, Discussion and Figures 1/7 were inspected. Mutant-region transfer did not restore photoautotrophy in D2 E69Q or V247M/A249T backgrounds. Incomplete segregation of deletion constructs is not a viable null phenotype or proof of a specific essential chemistry.

The current domain spans residues 195-385, so the predicted stop product retains part of it. Neither current database naming nor the frozen P71138 misannotation discussion supplies Slr2013 enzyme chemistry.

discussions.notes: Establish reconstructed-allele and reciprocal rescue results, protein product and abundance, and domain-selective experiments before assigning molecular edges. PS I-less comparisons also change the D2 background and are not attributed solely to Slr2013. Other members, later publications and raw spectroscopic traces remain incompletely reviewed; the imported family description and classification are preserved.
discussions.prompt: Resolve Slr2013 allele specificity and the contribution of DUF58 to the conditional photosynthetic phenotype.
discussions.rationale: The Y294Stop suppressor disrupts part of DUF58 and a C-terminal extension in a D2-mutant context. Whole-cell oxygen and growth rescue do not distinguish protein quality control, indirect expression effects or another mechanism. The observed phenotypes cannot be assigned to every DUF58 member.
